body: The navigator curriculum is built on the P-A-R-A-G-O-N framework. It covers scripts, checklists, mental health protocols, cultural sensitivity, and LGBTQ+ competency.

contacts.name: Q Center
contacts.note: 503-234-7837 — voicemail only, by appointment. Not a crisis line.

steps: Ask directly about a self-harm plan, means, and intent.
If yes: get staff immediately and call the crisis line.

body: Stop. Offer a choice. Offer water. Offer a break.

handbook.quote: Portland's wait is long, and that's not your fault. Let's get you IN the system.
Per ORS 807.040, [Chosen Name / Legal Name], DOB [date], is experiencing homelessness and residing at [shelter address]. Please waive ID fee. Staff signature, date.
We got [X] done. DHS will mail or call by [date]. Come back Tuesdays. Here's your paper with logins. Is it okay to leave a note for the next volunteer? What felt helpful?

items.v: Does the guest have safe mail? ROI signed for shelter mail?
Will the phone be on and charged for the DHS call? Minutes? Use the shelter phone with an 8–10am window?
Expired more than 1 year? Needs a birth certificate again? Fee waiver letter ready?
Can the guest read DHS letters? Offer to read them next time.
Manila envelope for papers? Photo only if the guest consents and has a phone.
DMV location: 122nd vs Mall 205? TriMet ticket needed?
EBT stolen? Lock it through ebtEDGE and request a replacement.
Check the notice: missed verification? Appeal within 45 days with Form 443.
CCO assigned? Health Share has better shelter clinic linkage.

Clarify that DHS, 211, and HMIS do NOT check warrants.
Offer privacy for the DMV photo.

One-page doc: legal name, DOB, last 4, HMIS ID, assessment date, phone, shelter.

intake.note: Fill this out on paper with the guest. Don't type a guest's information into the hub.

test.q: A guest wants to apply for SNAP and OHP. Where do they apply for both at once?
test.why: The ONE portal handles SNAP and OHP together.

test.q: The guest can't use the online portal. What is the paper backup for OHP?
test.why: OHP 7210 is the paper backup.

test.q: A guest's benefits were denied. Which form requests a hearing?
test.why: DHS Form 443 requests a hearing.

test.q: How long does a guest have to appeal a denial?
test.why: Appeals must be filed within 45 days of the denial notice.

test.q: Which form replaces a lost Social Security card?
test.why: SSA Form SS-5 replaces a Social Security card.

test.q: A guest says their EBT benefits were stolen. What do you help them do first?
o: Lock the card through ebtEDGE and request a replacement
Tell them to wait for next month
test.why: Lock the card in ebtEDGE, then request a replacement.

test.q: A guest's ID expired more than a year ago. What should you check?
o: Whether they need a birth certificate again
Nothing, an expired ID works the same
test.why: An ID expired over a year may need a new birth certificate.

test.q: When do you go through the interference checklist?
o: Only at a guest's first visit
Only when a guest was denied benefits
test.why: The checklist runs before ending every session.

test.q: A guest can't read the letters DHS sends them. What do you do?
o: Tell them to ask shelter staff
Offer to read the letters with them next time
Skip the letters and call DHS instead
Nothing, it isn't part of the session
test.why: Offer to read DHS letters with them next time.

test.q: When can you take a photo of a guest's papers?
o: Only if the guest consents and has a phone to keep it on
test.why: Photos only with consent, kept on the guest's own phone.

test.q: What goes in the volunteer notes about a guest's Social Security number?
o: The full number, so the next volunteer has it
Never the full number; the last 4 is optional on intake
test.why: Never the full SSN; the last 4 is optional.

test.q: Who picks today's goal on the intake sheet?
test.why: Today's goal is the guest's choice.

test.q: A guest's chosen name differs from their legal name. Which name do you use when talking with them?
test.why: Use the chosen name; the legal name is only for DHS and DMV forms.

test.q: Which of these does NOT go on the one-page housing packet?
test.why: The packet uses the last 4 only, never the full SSN.

test.q: A guest won't apply because they're afraid of a warrant. What can you tell them?
o: DHS, 211, and HMIS do not check for warrants
They should wait until the warrant clears
test.why: DHS, 211, and HMIS do not check warrants.

test.q: A guest shares something heavy and asks you to keep it secret. What do you do?
o: Promise to keep it secret so they keep talking
Stay, listen, and don't promise secrecy
Tell them to talk to someone else
test.why: Stay and listen, but never promise secrecy.

test.q: You ask directly and the guest says they have a plan to harm themselves. What comes next?
o: Get staff immediately, call the crisis line, and document the handoff
Give them the crisis number and let them go
Wait and see if it passes
test.why: Get staff, call the crisis line, and document the handoff.

test.q: A guest is getting upset. What are the de-escalation steps?
o: Raise your voice so they can hear you
Stop, offer a choice, offer water, offer a break
test.why: Stop, offer a choice, water, and a break.

test.q: What is the main message of the housing script?
o: Housing will come in a few weeks
The wait is long, it isn't their fault, and let's get them into the system
They should look for housing on their own
There's no point applying right now
test.why: Long wait, not their fault, get them in the system.

test.q: A guest needs a new DMV photo and is uneasy about how they'll look on their ID. What do you offer?
test.why: Offer privacy for the DMV photo.
